title: Tectorigenin Ameliorates Glucocorticoid-Induced Osteoporosis by Inhibiting the NF-kappaB Signal Pathway and Modulating Treg-Th17 Cell Balance.
authors: Peng, Peng; Wong, Puiian; Lv, Zheng; Tian, Jiaqing; He, Wei; Wei, Qiushi; Mo, Hui; He, Mincong
journal: Journal of cellular and molecular medicine
one_liner_zh: 该文研究药物Tectorigenin对糖皮质激素性骨质疏松的作用机制，涉及RANKL蛋白的分子对接，但核心是细胞信号通路与疾病治疗，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis is a common clinical orthopaedic disease, primarily due to excessive use of hormones. Tectorigenin has shown a certain efficacy in treating osteoporosis, but its underlying mechanisms are not yet fully understood. This study aimed to evaluate tectorigenin (TEC)'s potential in treating glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis (GIOP) by restoring the osteoclast-osteoblast balance. By employing molecular docking to study TEC-RANKL interaction and RNA sequencing to map TEC's anti-osteoporotic pathways, we conducted in vitro tests on TEC's effects on osteoclast differentiation, bone resorption, ROS production, and NF-kappaB activation. We performed a luciferase reporter assay for Nrf2 and NF-kappaB activities and evaluated TEC's in vivo efficacy using a GIOP mouse model with micro-CT and histomorphometric analyses, measuring serum RANKL levels and Treg/Th17 cell ratios. Docking analysis confirmed TEC's specific binding to RANKL and RNA sequencing showed TEC modulated osteoclast pathways. In vitro, TEC suppressed osteoclastogenesis, bone resorption, osteoclast gene expression, and ROS activity by downregulating NFATc1 and modulating NF-kappaB. The luciferase assay revealed TEC inhibited Nrf2 and influenced its interaction with NF-kappaB. In vivo, TEC protected against GIOP by balancing Th17/Treg cells to inhibit osteoclast differentiation and maintain bone volume. In conclusion, tectorigenin (TEC) shows promise in reducing osteoclastogenesis and preventing GIOP, making it a potential drug candidate for osteoporosis management.
abstract_zh: 糖皮质激素诱导的骨质疏松症是一种常见的临床骨科疾病，主要源于激素的过度使用。鸢尾苷元在治疗骨质疏松症方面显示出一定疗效，但其潜在机制尚未完全明了。本研究旨在评估鸢尾苷元（TEC）通过恢复破骨细胞-成骨细胞平衡来治疗糖皮质激素诱导的骨质疏松症（GIOP）的潜力。通过采用分子对接 (molecular docking) 研究TEC-RANKL相互作用，以及RNA测序 (RNA sequencing) 绘制TEC的抗骨质疏松通路，我们对TEC在破骨细胞分化、骨吸收、ROS产生及NF-kappaB激活方面的影响进行了体外测试。我们进行了针对Nrf2和NF-kappaB活性的荧光素酶报告基因检测，并使用GIOP小鼠模型通过micro-CT和组织形态计量学分析评估了TEC的体内疗效，测量了血清RANKL水平和Treg/Th17细胞比例。对接分析确认了TEC与RANKL的特异性结合，RNA测序显示TEC调节了破骨细胞通路。在体外，TEC通过下调NFATc1和调节NF-kappaB抑制了破骨细胞生成、骨吸收、破骨细胞基因表达及ROS活性。荧光素酶检测揭示TEC抑制了Nrf2并影响其与NF-kappaB的相互作用。在体内，TEC通过平衡Th17/Treg细胞来抑制破骨细胞分化并维持骨体积，从而对GIOP起到保护作用。总之，鸢尾苷元（TEC）在减少破骨细胞生成和预防GIOP方面显示出潜力，使其成为骨质疏松症管理的潜在候选药物。
